source.section: PDF page 60 Schedule CA (540) instructions, Line 5a and 5b (Military Retirement Exclusion, federal AGI limit 125,000 / 250,000, 20,000 cap); PDF page 6 and 55 What's New ('capped at $20,000 for ... spouses filing a joint return'); Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Married filing jointly, 60 and 58: both spouses receive uniformed-services retirement pay, 18,000 and 15,000 (33,000 together), and spouse 2 has wages 100,000; federal AGI = 133,000, under the 250,000 joint limit. The exclusion is one 20,000 cap for the joint return, not 20,000 each. Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 133,000.00. Federal taxable income = 133,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 101,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: Schedule CA (540) line 5 column B, Military Retirement Exclusion: federal AGI 133,000.00 does not exceed 250,000.00; military retirement pay 33,000.00, capped at 20,000.00 a return = 20,000.00. Schedule CA Part I line 27 column B = 20,000.00 = Form 540 line 14. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 133,000.00 - 20,000.00 = 113,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (married filing jointly, PDF page 13 chart) 11,412.00. Line 19 taxable income = 113,000.00 - 11,412.00 = 101,588.00. Tax on 101,588.00 by the projection's brackets: 22,158.00 x 1% = 221.58; 30,370.00 x 2% = 607.40; 30,376.00 x 4% = 1,215.04; 18,684.00 x 6% = 1,121.04; total 3,165.06. Line 31: Tax Rate Schedule Y (PDF page 75), from its printed base, gives 3,165.06. Line 32 exemption credits: federal AGI 133,000.00 is not more than 504,411.00, so no AGI limitation; line 7 personal 2 x 153 = 306.00; line 9 senior 0 x 153 = 0.00; line 32 = 306.00. Line 33 = 3,165.06 - 306.00 = 2,859.06; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 2,859.06. State income tax = 2,859.06.
